title: RBACv2 consistency validator, canary customer fallbacks, and admin UX toggles
creator: Alyssa Chen
description: Goal: Safely complete the RBAC v1 -> v2 migration for the control plane with minimal customer disruption. Deliverables: (1) a consistency validator service that detects divergence between v1 and v2 authorization decisions and KV state, (2) a canary-customer fallback flow and admin UI toggles to opt-out/rollback per account, (3) audit-log preservation strategy and SSO mapping verification runbook, and (4) end-to-end playbooks for dual-write backfill and emergency rollback.
acceptance_criteria: Consistency validator runs in production and reports divergence rate < 0.1% for canary cohort over 72h
Dual-write idempotent backfill completes for 95% of accounts within SLA window and logs per-account reconciliation events
Admin console exposes a secure toggle to opt a customer into RBACv2 with audit trail and RBACv1 fallback option
SSO/SAML mapping verification checklist executed against 10 enterprise pilot customers with zero mapping regressions
Audit logs for authorization decisions preserved and queryable for 90 days across cutover, including pre/post mapping context
tasks: Design and implement consistency-validator microservice (k8s deployment, leader election, rate-limited checks)
Add metrics and tracing hooks for 'auth_decision_source' tag and histograms for decision latency
Build idempotent backfill pipeline using changefeed snapshots + checkpointing; test on synthetic data
Create admin console toggles: 'Enable RBACv2 for account' and 'Fallback to RBACv1 (read-only)'; wire to audit log
Define canary cohorts (internal + 5 enterprise pilots) and rollout schedule with SLO gates
Update SSO mapping tests: automated end-to-end SAML handshake simulation and attribute mapping validation
Author customer comms and runbooks: pre-cutover checklist, migration FAQ, emergency rollback steps
Run chaos tests for partial failures: network partition, partial backfill failures, README for on-call
backfill_strategy: Backfill runs as a stateful job that reads changefeeds + a consistent snapshot from v1, writes to v2 through idempotent upserts, and emits per-account reconciliation events. Jobs checkpoint per-account and retry with exponential backoff; high-failure accounts move to manual remediation queue and generate a CS ticket template.
dual_write_plan: Enable dual-write behind a feature flag. Initially route 1% of traffic to v2 (shadow mode) while writing to both stores. After validator confirms parity for canary cohort, flip control-plane decision source for that cohort. Dual-write has per-request correlation ID for traceability to audit logs.
rollback_plan: Admin toggle to immediately switch an account back to RBACv1 policy decision path. For data-level rollback, maintain v1 authoritative store until cutover window + 30 days; provide migration-reversion job that uses reconciliation events to revert v2 mutations if required. Emergency steps documented with full playbook and communication templates.
audit_plan: Preserve raw authorization decision logs (v1 and v2) with context: user, request-id, timestamp, mapped roles/attributes, SAML assertion ID. Store immutable copies in the audit bucket with WORM retention 90d. Provide queryable index for quick forensics (by account, by request-id).
sso_mapping_verification: Create a deterministic SAML attribute simulator that exercises NameID and attribute mappings for common IdPs (Okta, Azure AD, Ping). Automate verification with CI gating that runs mapping checks when mapping rules change.
admin_ui_changes: New section under Settings > Security: 'RBAC Migration'. For each account show current status (v1|v2), last validated timestamp, divergence score, and actions: 'Enable RBACv2', 'Force Reconcile', 'Fallback to v1'. Actions require 2FA confirmation and generate an audit event.
communications: Draft customer email: timeline, opt-in testing instructions, safety guarantees and rollback assurances
Support playbook: canned responses for common issues (missing role mappings, 403 spikes, SSO login failures)
Engineering runbook: run commands to surface reconciliation errors and escalate steps

risk_assessment: Medium risk: primary risk vectors are SSO attribute mapping regressions causing 403s, and audit-log loss during cutover. Mitigations: automated mapping simulation, immutable audit copies, short canary windows, per-account fallback toggles, and manual remediation paths for high-value customers.
notes: This ticket coordinates engineering, security, product, and support. Keep tight coupling with Solutions Engineering for pilot onboarding and with Ops for runbook rehearsals. Schedule a dry-run drill with SRE and one pilot customer before any broad rollouts.
